title: IRGC Claims Destruction of AWS Bahrain Data Center
summary: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps \(IRGC\) claimed responsibility for destroying an Amazon Web Services data center in Bahrain, disrupting the AWS me-south-1 region. This incident demonstrates the vulnerability of centralized cloud infrastructure to geopolitical conflicts and physical attacks, posing risks for businesses relying on a single cloud provider in unstable regions. The attack targeted the BAH53 data center and its adjoining power substation, with damage occurring on July 16 and July 22, 2026, according to OSINT sources. The AWS Health Dashboard showed the me-south-1 region as unavailable since at least April 30, 2026.
context: AWS launched the me-south-1 region in Bahrain in 2019 to serve customers in the Middle East. The region originally consisted of three Availability Zones \(data centers\). This physical destruction of a data center highlights the risks of centralized cloud infrastructure in geopolitically sensitive areas.
discussion: Comments ranged from ironic humor \(comparing uptime reliability\) to geopolitical observations \(noting only the Tel Aviv region remains operational\). One user provided detailed OSINT mapping of the attacked facilities, while another highlighted the broader theme that centralization requires peace to function.
